A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we extend the previous work of \cite{MR3822846} for stationary flows to the non-stationary case.
we have proved the existence of a weak solution with the H^{2} velocity gradients for the Navier-Stokes equations with the slip boundary conditions.
we have proved the existence of the solution to a non-stationary Navier-Stokes equations with power-law stress tensor in a bounded two dimensional domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the case of power-law growth, the regularity of velocity gradients is not worse than the case of Newtonian fluids.
the H\"older exponent of the velocity gradients is strictly larger than the growth parameter.

the H\"older continuity of the velocity gradients is a direct consequence of the H\"older regularity of the pressure, which in turn is a by-product of a priori estimates for the solution of the linearised Navier-Stokes equations.
